detailed_rationale:
Radico Khaitan is India's leading premium-IMFL franchise (8PM Whisky, Magic Moments Vodka, Rampur Single Malt, Jaisalmer Gin), riding the country's multi-year premiumization trend as consumers trade up from cheap IMFL to prestige-and-above categories. Q1 FY27 results were genuinely strong: net revenue grew 11.8% YoY to Rs 1,683.7 crore, EBITDA jumped 50.9% to a record Rs 348.1 crore with margin expanding sharply to 20.7% from 15.3% a year earlier, and total comprehensive income rose 70.5% YoY to Rs 225.4 crore — the company's highest-ever quarterly profit. The engine is the Prestige & Above portfolio, which grew volumes 35.8% YoY to 5.22 million cases and now contributes 76.8% of IMFL revenue, up from 66.7% a year ago; management has responded by raising FY27 guidance to over 25% Prestige & Above volume growth with EBITDA margin sustained around 20%.

The quant scorecard flags this as expensive (value score 17/100, PE ~91x) with a stage-timing tag of 'Extended' (a large recent price run-up, +140% over 24 months) — both consistent with what the fundamentals show: this is an excellent, structurally-advantaged business whose success is already well recognized and priced. ROE (12.9%) and ROCE (18.4%) are solid but not exceptional in absolute terms, reflecting that Radico is still mid-cycle in converting premiumization volume growth into best-in-class capital returns (capacity investment and brand-building spend are ongoing).

Given that Prestige & Above is 76.8% of revenue and guided to grow 25%+ while the remaining ~23% (regular/economy IMFL) is a much slower, largely mature category, blended total-company growth should run somewhat below the segment-specific guidance number once the mix is weighted appropriately.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold on both axes. The business quality and premiumization tailwind are genuinely excellent, but the valuation (~91x, Extended stage) already reflects a great deal of that success, so there is no case for anything other than Hold — this is a high-conviction-business, full-price situation rather than a mispriced opportunity in either direction.
summary: Radico Khaitan is riding India's premiumization wave in spirits extremely well — record quarterly profit, EBITDA margin up nearly 550 basis points, and raised full-year guidance for its premium portfolio. The business quality is genuinely excellent, but at roughly 91x earnings and after a large recent price run-up, the valuation already prices in a great deal of continued flawless execution. We rate it a Hold.
positive_para: The premiumization shift is real, measurable, and accelerating — Prestige & Above volumes +35.8% YoY, now over three-quarters of IMFL revenue, driving genuine margin expansion (EBITDA margin +550bps YoY) rather than just volume-led growth, and management has raised rather than trimmed its forward guidance, a good signal of confidence in the trend's durability.
negative_para: At ~91x trailing earnings and after a 140% two-year price run, the stock has very little room for a premiumization slowdown, input-cost (ENA/grain, glass) inflation, or a state-level excise/regulatory disruption (a periodic risk across the IMFL sector) without a meaningful de-rating; ROE (12.9%) and ROCE (18.4%), while solid, are not yet at a level that fully justifies the multiple on capital-efficiency grounds alone.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~91x multiple prices in several more years of 20%+ EBITDA growth with continued margin expansion; the Prestige & Above guidance (25%+ volume growth) supports strong growth for that segment, but blended total-company growth should run somewhat lower once the slower-growing regular-IMFL portion of the business (still ~23% of revenue) is weighted in, meaning the multiple leaves limited margin for error on the pace of the mix shift.
